title: Screener: Self-supervised Pathology Segmentation in Medical CT Images
mechanism: Dense self-supervised features plus a density-based anomaly segmenter conditioned on learned masking-invariant dense features; the same pretraining also beats other SSL methods when fine-tuned supervised.
adaptation: One dense SSL run on the 159k pool gives (a) a dense-pretrained ResNet-34/ConvNeXt-T encoder for U-Net++ and (b) a label-free anomaly map; conditioning variable = cell layout/source embedding instead of position.
min_experiment: Arm dense SSL encoder + PF vs baseline PF and the MIM checkpoint, 5 seeds; metric CV crack IoU and inactive IoU; kill if crack gain < +0.012 and inactive < +0.02. About 60 GPU-h.
evidence: R: trained on > 30k unlabelled CT volumes; beats UVAS methods on four test sets (1,820 scans) and other SSL pretraining in supervised fine-tuning.
prior_overlap: Section 5 lists dense SSL objectives as not closed (MIM / DDeP only).
